A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed X-TURING in v2. All 16 pages of each version, including Appendices A-B, are readable and support comparison of methods, results, equations, and visual material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of three LLMs using 236 human judges and two LLM judges, alongside dialogue-history, topic, demographic, and case-study results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including the pass rates in Tables 1-2 and the supporting analyses.

M1.justification: The burst-messaging components, pseudo-dialogue generation algorithm, and appendix prompts are unchanged. Introducing mT for the final human-interaction length clarifies notation; both generation and final interaction still use 10-turn blocks.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same stated 25-topic evaluation, ping-pong and burst conversations, and short and prolonged interaction scenarios. Appendix B's generated topics also match. The missing topic-overview graphic changes documentation, without establishing changed evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-4, Claude-3-Sonnet, and Qwen-110B remain the evaluated models throughout the corresponding comparisons. Human reference conversations and GPT-4/Qwen-110B judges are retained; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The 100-turn reference history, 10/15-topic split between dialogue formats, 236 human judges, evaluation durations, and pass-rate metric remain unchanged. The option-randomization note moves from Table 8's caption to Appendix B.4 without changing the control.

E4.justification: The history-quantity ablation, topic and participant analyses, and both dialogue case studies are retained. Swapping the topic and participant subsections and adding a procedural diagram introduce no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information. Judge-count information and statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 match numerically, including GPT-4's human-judged average pass rates of 51.9%, 38.9%, and 13.3% at 3, 10, and 110 turns. The topic results, demographic data, and dialogue examples also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The dialogue-turn definitions, delay equation, pseudo-dialogue algorithm, and pass-rate formula are retained. The mT notation distinguishes the final interaction length without introducing a substantive derivation, assumption, or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about burst dialogue, efficient pseudo-dialogue evaluation, X-Turn Pass-Rate, and declining human likeness over longer interactions. Renaming the framework does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 changes the timing rationale: v1 assigns reading/thinking time to model generation and the added delay to typing; v2 describes that delay as mimicking all three. Interpretations of empirical results and the stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, while retaining the prompts and promise to release dialogue history after acceptance. Conversely, replacing the topic-overview graphic removes detailed evaluation-topic documentation that Appendix B's distinct generation-topic lists do not restore.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the visual-Turing-test citation to Geman et al. (2014) with Imanpour et al. (2024). It also removes the explicit claim of being first to address feasibility, retaining the broader positioning around efficient long-term evaluation.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and framework name, edits the abstract and introductory/method prose, updates affiliation and acknowledgment text, and swaps the topic-analysis and participant-distribution subsections. Most prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pseudo-dialogue pipeline diagram, recolors the demographic charts, expands a case-study caption, and relocates several displays. However, Figure 4 replaces v1's topic-overview chart with a duplicate of the performance plot shown in v2 Figure 7, retaining the incorrect topic-overview caption.

improvement.justification: The new pipeline diagram, code pointer, and more restrained novelty wording provide limited benefits. However, v2 Figure 4 removes the detailed evaluation-topic overview and substitutes a duplicate performance plot under a mismatched caption. With the scientific evidence otherwise unchanged, this concrete loss of experimental documentation outweighs the modest explanatory gains.
